world.era: far future — human interstellar colonies, roughly three thousand years after the Xenocide
world.setting: Milagre: a fenced Catholic, Portuguese-speaking colony town of a few hundred people on the forested world of Lusitania, ringed by capim grass and the pequenino forest. Whitewashed walls, a rain-wet praça, a cathedral, a xenobiology lab, one crowded family house — plus a university classroom on the ocean world Trondheim, and the long relativistic voyage between them.
world.register: intimate, domestic, grave. This is the anti-Ender's Game: no fleet, no battle room. A small town, a forest, a kitchen, a funeral held in the rain. Quiet rooms and trees that are people.

ender.name: Ender Wiggin
ender.role: The Speaker for the Dead. Biologically about thirty-five after decades of relativistic travel; the man who committed the Xenocide, travelling anonymously as the secular truth-teller his own book invented. Carries the hive queen's cocoon in a bag.
ender.look: A quiet man of about thirty-five, lean and unremarkable, dark short hair, plain grey traveller's coat over a white shirt, a worn satchel on one shoulder, watchful rather than commanding.

novinha.name: Novinha
novinha.role: Lusitania's xenobiologist. Orphan of Os Venerados, brilliant at thirteen, and the keeper of the secret the whole book is built on — she believes her research killed Pipo, and she marries to lock her files away from the man she loves.
novinha.look: A guarded woman in her forties, black hair pulled back tight, olive skin, a dark work dress under a pale lab coat, arms folded, grief worn as hardness.

marcao.name: Marcão
marcao.role: Marcos Ribeira. The colony's despised brute — huge, violent, dying of a genetic disease, sterile, and the only man in Milagre who knows every child in his house is Libo's and stays anyway. The Speaking is his.
marcao.look: An enormous man in his forties, thick-necked and heavy-shouldered, cropped dark hair and stubble, a sweat-stained work shirt and canvas trousers, hands like tools, shame worn as anger.

libo.name: Libo
libo.role: Pipo's son and successor as xenologer; Novinha's true love and the biological father of all six of her children. Killed by the pequeninos exactly as his father was.
libo.look: A warm, open-faced man in his thirties, curly brown hair, sleeves rolled, a field jacket with deep pockets, the easy posture of someone who is liked.

pipo.name: Pipo
pipo.role: The first xenologer of Lusitania. Sees in Novinha's data what the pequeninos are, tells them — and they honour him by opening him and planting him. The death that starts everything.
pipo.look: A kind, weathered man near sixty, grey receding hair, reading glasses, a heavy field coat over a cardigan, notebook always in hand.

miro.name: Miro
miro.role: Novinha's eldest son, secret xenologer, in love with Ouanda — until the Speaking tells him they are half-siblings.
miro.look: A serious young man of about twenty, dark tousled hair, a patched work jacket, wire fence cutters in his belt, eyes always on the treeline.

ouanda.name: Ouanda
ouanda.role: Libo and Bruxinha's daughter, field xenologer, Miro's love and — as the Speaking reveals — his half-sister.
ouanda.look: A composed young woman of about twenty, fair braided hair, a canvas field shirt and trousers, a specimen satchel across her chest.

bruxinha.name: Bruxinha
bruxinha.role: Libo's widow. For years she believed her husband's death was hers to mourn alone; the Speaking gives her the whole man, which is both a wound and a gift.
bruxinha.look: A small, soft-featured woman in her forties, dark hair loose to the shoulders, a plain mourning dress with a shawl, hands folded.

peregrino.name: Bishop Peregrino
peregrino.role: Milagre's bishop. Preaches against the Speaker from the pulpit, then watches the Speaking do the work his own church claims — and has a revelation.
peregrino.look: An austere churchman near seventy, bald with a fringe of white hair, a dark cassock with a pectoral cross, hands clasped, chin lifted.

human.name: Human
human.role: A pequenino — one of the 'piggies'. Small, furred, snouted, and a person. Ender grants him the third life with his own hands, and that killing becomes the treaty.
human.look: A small figure barely waist-high to a man, covered in short dark fur, a snouted face and wide-set eyes, no clothing but a woven grass cord; the rig can only approximate this — keep the silhouette small, hooded and non-human in scale.

valentine.name: Valentine
valentine.role: Ender's sister, and secretly the philosopher 'Demosthenes' whose Hierarchy of Foreignness gives humanity the words utlanning, framling, raman and varelse. The universe believes Demosthenes is an ancient figure.
valentine.look: A thoughtful woman in her thirties, light hair tied back, a scholar's dark coat over a high-collared shirt, a pen held like an argument.

plikt.name: Plikt
plikt.role: The professor on Trondheim who lays out Demosthenes' hierarchy to her class — the scene that hands the audience the book's moral vocabulary.
plikt.look: A sharp Nordic woman in her forties, pale cropped hair, a heavy knitted sweater under an academic gown, chalk in hand.

card.name: Orson Scott Card
card.role: The author. Show him ONLY when the hosts argue with the book's construction ('Card rigs the test') — a novelist at a desk deciding what the universe will allow, never as a character inside Milagre.
card.look: A bearded writer in his forties at a plain desk, glasses, a dark cardigan over a collared shirt, pen poised over a manuscript.

praca.look: The rain-wet praça of Milagre at dusk: whitewashed walls, cathedral steps, a few hundred colonists standing in drizzle. Where the Speaking happens.

forest.look: The pequenino forest beyond the fence — tall dark fathertrees, capim grass to the knee, everything alive and paired. Where Pipo and Libo were planted.

ribeiraHouse.look: The crowded Ribeira house: a scrubbed table, too many chairs, six children and one enormous silence.

lab.look: Novinha's xenobiology lab: sealed data files, tissue samples of the descolada, a bench lit too brightly at night.

cathedral.look: The cathedral and the monastery of the Filhos da Mente de Cristo — plain stone, candlelight, an order of married celibates teaching next door.

classroom.look: A university lecture room on the ocean world Trondheim: cold northern light, a professor pacing, the four categories chalked up in front of a class.

voyage.look: The long relativistic crossing between worlds — twenty-two years outside, a few weeks inside; the cocoon riding in a bag the whole way.

objects.why: The fathertree is the book's central object: the third life. A pequenino who is honoured is opened and planted, and a tree grows out of him. Every 'murder' in the book is somebody trying to make one of these.
The Speaking is a funeral rite. The whole film happens over the dead: Pipo, Libo, Marcão — and the buggers.
The Ribeira household is the crime scene. Six children, one secret, one man eating the town's contempt to hold it up.
Novinha's sealed research files — the thing she marries a brutal man to lock away. The plot's actual motive is a set of documents.
Starways Congress rules, the fence, and Demosthenes' four categories. The hierarchy of foreignness is a legal instrument, not a description — this is the diagram the film owes the audience.
Marcão's sterility and his disease; Novinha's love for Libo; the cocoon Ender carries. The body keeps every secret in this book.
Marriage as a lock. Spousal privilege is what seals the files — the wedding IS the key, which is the single most quotable idea in the episode.

The fenced colony: a few hundred people walled off from a forest of people they cannot read. NOTE — we have no fence/gate icon; the fence is the book's defining structure and is worth drawing (Phase 4).
The Hive Queen and the Hegemon — the anonymous book Ender wrote that turned him into history's monster and invented the Speakers.
Relativistic distance: twenty-two years of travel, three thousand years of consequence. Time is the book's cruellest instrument.
The Xenocide itself — the crime the whole moral apparatus was built to apologise for.

Rain on the praça. The Speaking happens in a drizzle and the book keeps returning to that grey wet light. NOTE — the descolada (a virus that rewrites genomes and pairs every species on Lusitania) has no icon; it is the story's engine and is worth drawing (Phase 4).

spine.claim: A fenced Catholic colony lives beside a forest of aliens it cannot read, and the man who once wiped out a species arrives to perform a ritual that tells the whole truth about a dead man.
Pipo's death was not a murder but the pequeninos' highest honour — the third life — and atrocity and reverence turn out to be the identical physical act across a species line.
Demosthenes' four categories are a permissions system, not a taxonomy: 'varelse' is the label that makes killing allowable, and it is always assigned by the side that failed to understand.
Novinha's protective secret needed a whole family to hold it up — and the Speaking detonates it in one afternoon, costing exactly what the lie was buying.
Ender puts the knife in Human himself, and the same act that was xenocide becomes a treaty; the redemption is not that he stopped killing, but that he finally knows what he is doing.
